title: Create the ontology from a notebook
text: Build a Fabric data agent with an ontology Create the ontology from a notebook This lab focuses on building and using a Fabric data agent grounded in an ontology. To maximize your time on those tasks, you'll use a notebook that automates the ontology creation process, including setting up the lakehouse, eventhouse, entity types, data bindings, and relationships. The Lamna Healthcare ontology includes sample data representing hospitals, departments, rooms, patients, and vital sign monitoring equipment. Note : If you want to learn how to build ontologies step-by-step, see the exercises on creating an ontology manually or generating an ontology from a semantic model. The notebook contains detailed markdown cells explaining each step. It will: What to expect when the notebook runs As the notebook executes, watch for these success indicators in the cell outputs: Troubleshooting : If Step 4 shows "❌ FAILED", verify tenant settings are enabled and try re-running the notebook. Important : After the notebook completes, Fabric processes the data bindings and builds the graph model in the background. This processing typically completes in a few minutes, depending on capacity load and complexity. This is a one-time setup process. Once complete, the ontology remains responsive. To check if data is ready, open the LamnaHealthcareOntology item, select an entity type (for example, Departments), and select Entity type overview . If you see "Setting up your ontology" or "Updating your ontology", wait on the page — it will automatically update when the preview experience finishes loading. Once entity instances appear, you can continue to the next section.

title: Publish and share the data agent
text: Build a Fabric data agent with an ontology Publish and share the data agent Publish the data agent to create a stable version that colleagues can query. Publish the data agent Queries the Lamna Healthcare ontology to answer questions about patient room assignments, department occupancy, and vital sign equipment allocation. For this exercise, keep it off. Publishing creates two versions: Share the data agent There are two steps to sharing a data agent: granting access, then sharing the link. Step 1: Grant access A Grant people access dialog opens. Step 2: Share the link A Create and send link dialog opens with options to copy the link, share by email, or share by Teams. Important : The link only works for people you've already granted access to in Step 1. Recipients must also have Read permission on the LamnaHealthcareOntology item, LamnaHealthcareLH lakehouse, and LamnaHealthcareEH eventhouse. For full details on permission requirements by data source type, see Fabric data agent sharing and permission management.

title: Simplify the data schema
text: 'Prepare a semantic model for AI in Microsoft Fabric' Simplify the data schema Hiding technical fields helps Copilot focus on business-relevant data and produce more accurate responses. In this section, you use the Prep for AI dialog to deselect surrogate keys, sort columns, and ETL metadata from the AI data schema. Deselected fields include surrogate keys ( CustomerKey , ProductKey ), sort helper columns ( Day (Sort Order) , Month (Sort Order) ), ETL metadata ( LoadDate , SourceSystem ), and internal identifiers ( SalesOrderLineNumber ). Deselecting LoadDate also removes its auto-generated Date Hierarchy, which is expected — the dedicated Date table handles time-based analysis.

title: Add synonyms with linguistic modeling
text: 'Prepare a semantic model for AI in Microsoft Fabric' Add synonyms with linguistic modeling Synonyms help Copilot and Q&A interpret natural language variations for field and measure names. In this section, you add synonyms to key fields using the Q&A linguistic modeling setup. Notice the Suggestions and add item . When you add the suggested synonym, you are prompted to share approved synonyms with your entire org. This choice helps provide consistency across your organization and support an enterprise ontology. Select OK to share the synonym. Publish and validate changes Publishing the report makes the semantic model available in the Power BI service, where you can test with Copilot and mark the model as approved. Test with Copilot Validating your AI preparation confirms that Copilot uses the correct fields, measures, and verified answers. In this section, you test the published model with Copilot in the Power BI service, use HCAAT diagnostics to inspect Copilot's reasoning, and mark the model as Approved for Copilot. Copilot should return the predefined card visual showing total sales, rather than generating a new response. Copilot should return the bar chart visual you created the verified answer for. Based on your AI instructions, Copilot should use the Profit Margin measure rather than the Profit measure. The synonym "profitability" should map correctly to Profit Margin . Select the HCAAT link again and verify that Copilot uses City and Total Sales without referencing any surrogate keys or ETL columns. Mark the model as Approved for Copilot Approving a semantic model tells your organization that it's been validated and is ready for AI consumption. In this task, you mark the published semantic model as Approved for Copilot. Note : You might need to refresh the browser tab to see the semantic model. Your semantic model will have improved visibility in search results. It also removes the warning in standalone Copilot in Power BI that your organization hasn't approved the data.

title: Preview Data in Power Query Editor
text: Get data in Power BI Preview Data in Power Query Editor This task introduces the Power Query Editor and allows you to review and profile the data. This helps you determine how to clean and transform the data later. You'll also review both dimension tables prefixed with "Dim" and fact tables prefixed with "Fact". The DimEmployee table in the SQL Server database stores one row for each employee. A subset of the rows from this table represents the salespeople, which will be relevant to the model you’ll develop. These five columns represent relationships to other tables in the database. They can be used to join tables together. You’ll join these tables later in the Load Transformed Data in Power BI Desktop lab. Note : When the distinct and unique counts are the same, it means the column contains unique values. When modeling, it’s important that some model tables have unique columns. These unique columns can be used to create one-to-many relationships, which you'll do in the Model Data in Power BI Desktop lab. The DimProduct table contains one row per product sold by the company. The DimReseller table contains one row per reseller. Resellers sell, distribute, or value add to the Adventure Works products. Notice the data quality issue: there are two labels for warehouse ( Warehouse , and the misspelled Ware House ). The DimSalesTerritory table contains one row per sales region, including Corporate HQ (headquarters). Regions are assigned to a country, and countries are assigned to groups. In the Model Data in Power BI Desktop lab, you’ll create a hierarchy to support analysis at region, country, or group level. The FactResellerSales table contains one row per sales order line—a sales order contains one or more line items. Missing TotalProductCost column values is a data quality issue.

title: Configure the Sales query
text: Clean, transform, and load data in Power BI Configure the Sales query In this task, you'll configure the Sales query. Note : You may recall in the Prepare Data in Power BI Desktop lab that a small percentage of FactResellerSales rows had missing TotalProductCost values. The DimProduct column has been included to retrieve the product standard cost column to assist fixing the missing values. if [TotalProductCost] = null then [OrderQuantity] [StandardCost] else [TotalProductCost] Note : You can copy the expression from the Snippets.txt file in the 02-transform-data folder. This expression tests if the TotalProductCost value is missing. If missing, it produces a value by multiplying the OrderQuantity value by the StandardCost value; otherwise, it uses the existing TotalProductCost value. Configuring the correct data type is important. When the column contains numeric value, it’s also important to choose the correct type if you expect to perform mathematic calculations. The fixed decimal number data type allows for 19 digits, and allows for more precision to avoid rounding errors. It’s important to use the fixed decimal number type for financial values, or rates (like exchange rates). In the status bar, verify that the query has 10 columns and 999+ rows. title: Create model relationships
text: Configure a semantic model in Power BI Create model relationships In this task, you'll create model relationships. The file was configured to not identify relationships between tables, which isn't the default setting, but is recommended to prevent extra work creating the correct relationships for your model. The labs use a shorthand notation to reference a field. It will look like this: Product Category . In this example, Product is the table name and Category is the field name. The issue is that the table is based on fields from different tables. The expectation is that each product category displays the sales for that category. However, because there isn't a model relationship between these tables, the Sales table isn't filtered. You'll now add a relationship to propagate filters between the tables. You can interpret many of the relationship properties by looking at the relationship line in the diagram: - Cardinality is represented by the 1 and (\ ) indicators. - Filter direction is represented by the arrow head. - A solid line represents an active relationship; a dotted line represents an inactive relationship. Tip: If you hover the cursor over the relationship to highlight the related columns. Filters applied to the Product table now propagate to the Sales table.

title: Create a many-to-many relationship
text: Configure a semantic model in Power BI Create a many-to-many relationship In this task, you'll create a many-to-many relationship between the Salesperson table and the Sales table. The table visual displays sales made by each salesperson. However, there's another relationship between salespeople and sales. Some salespeople belong to one, two, or possibly more sales regions. In addition, sales regions can have multiple salespeople assigned to them. From a performance management perspective, a salesperson's sales (based on their assigned territories) need to be analyzed and compared with sales targets. You'll create relationships to support this analysis in the next exercise. The SalespersonRegion table can be considered to be a bridging table. Consider that the Salesperson table filters the Sales table. It also filters the SalespersonRegion table, but it doesn't continue by propagating filters to the Region table (the arrowhead is pointing the wrong direction). The issue now relates to the fact that there are two possible filter propagation paths between the Salesperson and Sales tables. This ambiguity is internally resolved, based on a "least number of tables" assessment. To be clear, you shouldn't design models with this type of ambiguity—the issue will be addressed in part later in this lab, and by the completion of the Create DAX Calculations in Power BI Desktop lab. Filter propagation will now follow the only active path. It's a common observation of a many-to-many relationship due to the double, triple, etc. counting of regional sales results. Consider Brian Welcker, the second salesperson listed. His sales amount equals the total sales amount. It's the correct result due to the fact that he's the Director of Sales; his sales are measured by the sales of all regions. While the many-to-many relationship is now working, it's now not possible to analyze sales made by a salesperson (because the relationship is inactive). You'll be able to reactivate the relationship when you introduce a calculated table that will allow analyzing sales made in the sales region(s) assigned to the salesperson (for performance analysis) in the Create DAX Calculations in Power BI Desktop lab. The renamed table now reflects its purpose: it's used to report and analyze the performance of salespeople based on the sales of their assigned sales regions.

title: Create the Salesperson calculated table
text: Create DAX calculations in semantic models Create the Salesperson calculated table In this task, you'll create the Salesperson calculated table (that will have a direct relationship to the Sales table). A calculated table is created by first entering the table name, followed by the equals symbol (=), followed by a DAX formula that returns a table. The table name can't already exist in the data model. You enter a valid DAX formula in the formula bar . The formula bar includes features like auto-complete, Intellisense and color-coding, which allow you to quickly and accurately enter the formula. Note : For your convenience, all DAX definitions in this lab can be copied from the snippets file, located in the 04-dax-calculations\Snippets.txt file. This table definition creates a copy of the Salesperson (Performance) table. It copies the data only, however model properties like visibility, formatting, and others aren't copied. Note : Calculated tables are defined by using a DAX formula that returns a table. It's important to understand that calculated tables increase the size of the data model because they materialize and store values. Also, they're recomputed whenever formula dependencies are refreshed, as will be the case for this data model when new (future) date values are loaded into tables. Unlike Power Query-sourced tables, calculated tables can't be used to load data from external data sources. They can only transform data based on what has already been loaded into the data model. The labs use a shorthand notation to reference a field. It will look like this: Salesperson EmployeeKey . In this example, Salesperson is the table name and EmployeeKey is the column name. You may recall that descriptions appear as tooltips in the Data pane whenever the user hovers their cursor over a table or field. The data model now provides two alternatives when analyzing salespeople. The Salesperson table allows analyzing sales made by a salesperson, while the Salesperson (Performance) table allows analyzing sales made in the sales region(s) assigned to the salesperson.

title: Create the Date table
text: Create DAX calculations in semantic models Create the Date table In this task, you'll create the Date table. dax Date = CALENDARAUTO(6) The CALENDARAUTO function returns a single-column table comprising date values. The "auto" behavior scans all data model date columns to determine the earliest and latest date values stored in the data model. It then creates one row for each date within this range, extending the range in either direction to ensure full years of data is stored. This function can take a single optional argument that is the last month number of a year. When omitted, the value is 12, meaning that December is the last month of the year. In this case, 6 is entered, meaning that June is the last month of the year.

title: Create simple measures
text: Create DAX calculations in semantic models Create simple measures In this task, you'll create simple measures. Simple measures aggregate values in a single column or count rows of a table. Visible numeric columns allow report authors at report design time to decide how column values will summarize (or not). However, it can result in inappropriate reporting. Some data modelers don't like leaving things to chance, so they choose to hide these columns and instead expose aggregation logic defined in measures. It's the approach you'll now take in this lab. DAX Avg Price = AVERAGE(Sales[Unit Price]) It's not possible to modify the aggregation behavior of a measure. The DISTINCTCOUNT function used in the Orders measure counts orders only once (ignoring duplicates). The COUNTROWS function used in the Order Lines measure operates over a table. In this case, the number of orders is calculated by counting the distinct SalesOrderNumber column values, while the number of order lines is simply the number of table rows (each row is a line of an order). The Unit Price column is no longer available to report authors. They must use the pricing measures you've added to the model. This design approach ensures that report authors won't inappropriately aggregate prices, for example, by summing them.

title: Manipulate filter context
text: Modify DAX filter context in Power BI Manipulate filter context In this task, you'll create several measures with DAX expressions that use the CALCULATE function to manipulate filter context. The CALCULATE function is a powerful function you can use to manipulate the filter context. The first argument takes an expression or a measure (a measure is just a named expression). Subsequent arguments allow modifying the filter context. Note : For your convenience, all DAX definitions in this lab can be copied from the C:\Users\Student\Downloads\05-modify-dax-filter-context\Snippets.txt file. dax Sales All Region = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), REMOVEFILTERS(Region) ) The REMOVEFILTERS function removes active filters. It can take either no arguments, or a table, a column, or multiple columns as its argument. In this formula, the measure evaluates the sum of the Sales column in a modified filter context, which removes any filters applied to the columns of the Region table. The new measure is yet to deliver a useful result. When the sales for a group, country, or region is divided by this value it will produce a useful ratio known as "percent of grand total". Tip: To replace the existing formula, first copy the snippet. Then, select inside the formula bar and press Ctrl+A to select all text. Then, press Ctrl+V to paste the snippet to overwrite the selected text. Then press Enter . dax Sales % All Region = DIVIDE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), REMOVEFILTERS(Region) ) ) The measure has been renamed to accurately reflect the updated formula. The DIVIDE function divides the sum of the Sales column (not modified by filter context) by the sum of the Sales column in a modified context, which removes any filters applied to the Region table. dax Sales % Country = DIVIDE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), REMOVEFILTERS(Region[Region]) ) ) The difference is that the denominator modifies the filter context by removing filters on the Region column of the Region table, not all columns of the Region table. That means that any filters applied to the group or country columns are preserved. It will achieve a result that represents the sales as a percentage of country. You might recall that only the United States has multiple regions. All other countries comprise a single region, which explains why they're all 100 percent. dax Sales % Country = IF( ISINSCOPE(Region[Region]), DIVIDE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), REMOVEFILTERS(Region[Region]) ) ) ) The IF function uses the ISINSCOPE function to test whether the region column is the level in a hierarchy of levels. When true, the DIVIDE function is evaluated. When false, BLANK is returned because the region column isn't in scope. dax Sales % Group = DIVIDE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), REMOVEFILTERS( Region[Region], Region[Country] ) ) ) To achieve sales as a percentage of group, two filters can be applied to effectively remove the filters on two columns. dax Sales % Group = IF( ISINSCOPE(Region[Region]) ISINSCOPE(Region[Country]), DIVIDE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), REMOVEFILTERS( Region[Region], Region[Country] ) ) ) ) The measures added to the Sales table have modified filter context to achieve hierarchical navigation. Notice that the pattern to achieve the calculation of a subtotal requires removing some columns from the filter context, and to arrive at a grand total, all columns must be removed.

title: Create a YTD measure
text: Use DAX time intelligence functions in Power BI Create a YTD measure In this task, you'll create a sales year-to-date (YTD) measure by using time intelligence functions. dax Sales YTD = TOTALYTD( SUM(Sales[Sales]), 'Date'[Date], "6-30" ) The TOTALYTD function evaluates an expression—in this case the sum of the Sales column—over a given date column. The date column must belong to a date table marked as a date table. The function can also take a third optional argument representing the last date of a year. The absence of this date means that December 31 is the last date of the year. For Adventure Works, June is in the last month of their year, and so "6-30" is used. The TOTALYTD function performs filter manipulation, specifically time filter manipulation. For example, to compute YTD sales for September 2017 (the third month of the fiscal year), all filters on the Date table are removed and replaced with a new filter of dates commencing at the beginning of the year (July 1, 2017) and extending through to the last date of the in-context date period (September 30, 2017). Many time intelligence functions are available in DAX to support common time filter manipulations.

title: Create a YoY growth measure
text: Use DAX time intelligence functions in Power BI Create a YoY growth measure In this task, you'll create a sales YoY growth measure by using a variable. Variables help you simplify the formula and are more efficient if using the logic multiple times within a formula. Variables are declared with a unique name, and the measure expression must then be output after the RETURN keyword. Unlike some other coding language variables, DAX variables can only be used within the single formula. dax Sales YoY Growth = VAR SalesPriorYear = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), PARALLELPERIOD( 'Date'[Date], -12, MONTH ) ) RETURN SalesPriorYear The SalesPriorYear variable is assigned an expression that calculates the sum of the Sales column in a modified context. That context uses the PARALLELPERIOD function to shift 12 months back from each date in filter context. Now that the "difficult part" of the formula has been tested, you can overwrite the measure with the final formula that computes the growth result. dax Sales YoY Growth = VAR SalesPriorYear = CALCULATE( SUM(Sales[Sales]), PARALLELPERIOD( 'Date'[Date], -12, MONTH ) ) RETURN DIVIDE( (SUM(Sales[Sales]) - SalesPriorYear), SalesPriorYear ) The YoY growth measure identifies almost 400 percent (or 4x) increase of sales during the same period of the previous year.

text: Create visual calculations in Power BI Desktop Add calculations DAX Profit = [Sum of Sales] - [Sum of Cost] Versus Previous compares a value to a preceding value, so we see the Profit compared to the previous value for Year. title: Create a forecast
text: Perform analytics in Power BI Create a forecast In this task, you'll create a forecast to determine possible future sales revenue. When forecasting over a time line, you'll need at least two cycles (years) of data to produce an accurate and stable forecast. If the Forecast section isn't available, it’s probably because the visual hasn’t been correctly configured. Forecasting is only available when two conditions are met: the axis has a single field of type date, and there’s only one value field. The gray area represents the confidence. The wider the confidence, the less stable—and therefore the less accurate—the forecast is likely to be. When you know the length of the cycle, in this case annual, you should enter the seasonality points. Sometimes it could be weekly (7), or monthly (30).

title: Enforce row-level security
text: Secure data access in Power BI Enforce row-level security In this task, you'll enforce row-level security to ensure a salesperson can only see sales made in their assigned region(s). You may recall that Michael Blythe is assigned to three sales regions: US Northeast, US Central, and US Southeast. DAX [UPN] = USERPRINCIPALNAME() USERPRINCIPALNAME() is a Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) function that returns the name of the authenticated user. It means that the Salesperson (Performance) table will filter by the User Principal Name (UPN) of the user querying the model. This configuration results in using the Salespeople role and impersonating the user with your Michael Blythe’s name. Note: When the Power BI Desktop file is published to the Power BI service, you’ll need to complete a post-publication task to map security principals to the Salespeople role. Tables, Rows, Columns, and Grain A table is a relation containing rows and attributes. Before writing a query, identify the grain : what one row represents. Examples: Why grain matters Many SQL bugs are not syntax bugs. They are grain mistakes that silently multiply rows or produce incorrect aggregates. Before JOIN , GROUP BY , or a window function, ask: What does one input row represent, and what should one output row represent?

title: 3. Logical Query Processing Order
text: 🧱 01 — SQL Foundations — Complete Reference Distinguish logical query meaning, physical execution, filtering and grouping. 3. Logical Query Processing Order A useful conceptual order is: FROM / JOIN → WHERE → GROUP BY → HAVING → SELECT → DISTINCT → ORDER BY → LIMIT/OFFSET Window functions are evaluated after the grouped result exists, which is why they can use aggregate results but generally cannot be used directly in WHERE . This order explains common patterns such as filtering a window-function result in an outer query or CTE.

Determinism and Ordering A result set is not guaranteed to have a meaningful order unless ORDER BY is specified. Likewise, operations such as ROW NUMBER() require an ordering definition if deterministic ranking is expected. Avoid assuming physical table order, insertion order, or clustered storage order is a logical ordering guarantee.

title: 14. Interview Traps
text: 🧱 01 — SQL Foundations — Complete Reference Distinguish logical query meaning, physical execution, filtering and grouping. 14. Interview Traps Q: Why can WHERE not normally contain an aggregate like SUM(amount) 1000 ? Because WHERE filters rows before grouping/aggregation. Use HAVING for group-level aggregate filters. Q: Why can a LEFT JOIN unexpectedly behave like an inner join? A predicate on the right-side table placed in WHERE can eliminate the NULL -extended rows created by the left join. Move the predicate into the ON condition when preserving unmatched left rows is required. Q: Why does COUNT( ) differ from COUNT(column) ? COUNT( ) counts rows; COUNT(column) counts non-NULL values of that column.

title: 1. سير عمل الاستكشاف الواقعي (The Real-World EDA Workflow)
text: 🧩 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling — Complete Reference Inspect keys, relationships, constraints and missing values before querying. 1. سير عمل الاستكشاف الواقعي (The Real-World EDA Workflow) عندما تدخل Database جديدة في شغل حقيقي، لا تبدأ مباشرة بـ SELECT على كل شيء. فكّر بالترتيب: Database ↓ 1. Discover tables & relationships ↓ 2. Inspect schema / ERD ↓ 3. Identify PKs & FKs ↓ 4. Understand data types & constraints ↓ 5. Sample rows ↓ 6. Check NULLs / missing / suspicious codes ↓ 7. Summarize distributions ↓ 8. Explore relationships between variables ↓ 9. Build intermediate datasets when useful ↓ 10. Answer the business question مثال واقعي: Student Analytics Database تخيل أنك انضممت لفريق BI في جامعة، وعندك tables مثل students ، enrollments ، courses ، departments . قبل أن تسأل "ما متوسط الـ GPA؟" لازم تعرف: ما هو الـgrain لكل table؟ ما هو الـprimary key؟ ما هي الـforeign keys؟ هل GPA يمكن أن يكون NULL؟ هل 0 GPA حقيقي أم missing code؟ Core principle: فهم الـ semantics والـ schema يسبق التحليل.

title: 2. استكشاف محتوى الـDatabase
text: 🧩 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling — Complete Reference Inspect keys, relationships, constraints and missing values before querying. 2. استكشاف محتوى الـDatabase 2.1 Database Client الـ database client هو البرنامج الذي تتصل من خلاله بالـ database وتنفذ SQL وتفحص الـ schema. يساعدك في اكتشاف Table names، Column names، Data types، Constraints، Relationships. في الشغل الحقيقي، ارجع أيضًا إلى الـ ERD والـ data dictionary والـ database documentation؛ لا تعتمد على SQL وحده لفهم business meaning. 2.2 Sampling Rows SELECT customer id, country, signup date FROM customers LIMIT 10; مهم الـ rows ليست مرتبة افتراضيًا. إذا كنت تريد ترتيبًا محددًا: SELECT FROM customers ORDER BY signup date DESC LIMIT 10; LIMIT يقلل عدد الصفوف المعروضة؛ لا يعني بالضرورة أن database قرأت فقط هذه الصفوف منطقياً في كل execution plan.

title: 3. أساسيات NULL
text: 🧩 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling — Complete Reference Inspect keys, relationships, constraints and missing values before querying. 3. أساسيات NULL NULL تعني unknown / missing value ، وليست رقمًا ولا string فارغًا. 3.1 Correct NULL syntax ❌ خطأ: WHERE salary = NULL — ✅ صحيح: WHERE salary IS NULL وللبحث عن القيم الموجودة: WHERE salary IS NOT NULL 3.2 COUNT(\ ) vs COUNT(column) COUNT( ) يعد عدد الصفوف . بينما COUNT(salary) يعد عدد القيم غير NULL فقط. إذن: Missing salary = COUNT( ) - COUNT(salary) مثال واقعي: Data quality check SELECT COUNT( ) AS total rows, COUNT(student id) AS student id present, COUNT(gpa) AS gpa present, COUNT( ) - COUNT(gpa) AS missing gpa FROM students; 3.3 COUNT(DISTINCT column) COUNT(DISTINCT country) يعد عدد القيم المختلفة غير NULL . لكن SELECT DISTINCT country FROM students; يمكن أن يظهر NULL كواحد من القيم المميزة. Exam / interview trap: DISTINCT قد يعرض NULL، بينما COUNT(DISTINCT column) لا يعد NULL.

title: 4. المفاتيح والعلاقات (Keys & Relationships)
text: 🧩 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling — Complete Reference Inspect keys, relationships, constraints and missing values before querying. 4. المفاتيح والعلاقات (Keys & Relationships) 4.1 Primary Key (PK) الـ Primary Key هو العمود/مجموعة الأعمدة التي uniquely identify كل row. خصائصه: Unique، Not NULL، يحدد هوية الصف. 4.2 Foreign Key (FK) الـ Foreign Key هو column يشير إلى key في table أخرى، وغالبًا إلى primary key. students --------- id (PK) ↑ │ FK │ enrollments ------------ student id (FK) الـ FK يساعد على فرض referential integrity : القيمة الموجودة في الـ child table يجب أن تتوافق مع قيمة مسموحة في الـ referenced table، أو تكون NULL إذا كان العمود يسمح بذلك. 4.3 Self-reference employees --------- id PK manager id FK → employees.id يسمح بتمثيل hierarchy (CEO ← Manager ← Employees). 4.4 الـFK ليس شرطًا لعمل JOIN SELECT FROM company c JOIN fortune500 f ON c.ticker = f.ticker; إذا لم توجد FK بين الجدولين، فهذا لا يمنع الـ JOIN. الفرق أن database لا تفرض نفس referential constraint على ticker . Key distinction: JOIN هو query operation؛ FOREIGN KEY هو database constraint.

title: 5. قيود الأعمدة (Column Constraints)
text: 🧩 02 — Database, Schema & Data Modeling — Complete Reference Inspect keys, relationships, constraints and missing values before querying. 5. قيود الأعمدة (Column Constraints) الـ constraints تحدد ما القيم المسموح بها. UNIQUE كل قيمة غير NULL يجب أن تكون مختلفة: email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL العمود لا يقبل NULL: student id INT NOT NULL CHECK يفرض business/data rule: CHECK (gpa = 0 AND gpa أو CHECK (end date = start date) PK / FK PK يحدد row uniquely، FK يربط row بـ referenced row ويحافظ على referential integrity. Important: Constraints are not the same as data types. Data type يحدد طبيعة القيم التي يمكن تخزينها؛ constraint يضيف قواعد إضافية على تلك القيم.

title: 9. The Safe Aggregation Pattern
text: 🔗 05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning — Complete Reference Predict JOIN cardinality and prevent duplicated measures. 9. The Safe Aggregation Pattern Aggregate each many-side independently before joining when the business grain requires it. WITH order totals AS ( SELECT customer id, SUM(order amount) AS total orders FROM orders GROUP BY customer id ), payment totals AS ( SELECT customer id, SUM(payment amount) AS total payments FROM payments GROUP BY customer id ) SELECT c.customer id, COALESCE(o.total orders, 0) AS total orders, COALESCE(p.total payments, 0) AS total payments FROM customers c LEFT JOIN order totals o ON o.customer id = c.customer id LEFT JOIN payment totals p ON p.customer id = c.customer id;

title: 17. Interview Traps
text: 🔗 05 — JOINs & Relationship Reasoning — Complete Reference Predict JOIN cardinality and prevent duplicated measures. 17. Interview Traps Q: Why did my total revenue double after adding a JOIN? Likely row multiplication caused by a one-to-many or many-to-many relationship. Inspect the grain and cardinality instead of adding DISTINCT blindly. Q: JOIN or EXISTS for "customers who placed at least one order"? EXISTS is often the clearer expression because the requirement is existence, not returning order columns. Q: Can LEFT JOIN increase rows? Yes. LEFT describes preservation of left rows; it does not guarantee one output row per left row.

title: 18. Interview Traps
text: 📊 06 — Aggregation & Grouping — Complete Reference Choose the grouping grain and define a correct KPI denominator. 18. Interview Traps Q: Why is COUNT( ) sometimes wrong for "customers"? Because rows may represent transactions, not customers. Use the count that matches the business entity, often COUNT(DISTINCT customer id) . Q: Why did SUM(revenue) increase after a JOIN? Usually because the JOIN multiplied fact rows before aggregation. Q: GROUP BY or window function? Use GROUP BY when you need fewer rows at a new grain. Use a window function when you need an analytical calculation while preserving row detail.

title: 11. Real BI Use Case — Student Analytics
text: 07 — Subqueries & CTEs — Complete Reference Choose subqueries, EXISTS and CTEs from result shape and dependency. 11. Real BI Use Case — Student Analytics Business question: Which students are currently active and have completed more credits than the average active student? WITH active students AS ( SELECT student id, earned hours FROM enrollment snapshot WHERE status code = 'ACTIVE' ), avg hours AS ( SELECT AVG(earned hours) AS avg earned hours FROM active students ) SELECT s.student id, s.earned hours FROM active students s CROSS JOIN avg hours a WHERE s.earned hours a.avg earned hours; The CTE separates population definition from benchmark calculation , making the logic easier to validate.

title: 🎯 الهدف من الدليل
text: 📚 09 — Window Functions — Complete Reference Distinguish partition, order and frame while preserving row detail. 🎯 الهدف من الدليل مرجع شامل للمذاكرة السريعة والعميقة لـ SQL Window Functions : المفهوم، الصياغة، ORDER BY ، PARTITION BY ، Fetching، Ranking، Paging، Window Frames، الحالات الخاصة، والأخطاء الشائعة. الفكرة الذهبية: Window Function تحسب نتيجة اعتمادًا على مجموعة من الصفوف المرتبطة بالـ current row، مع إبقاء الصفوف الأصلية موجودة . الموضوع اتقسم لـ 8 صفحات فرعية حسب الفرع، عشان يبقى سهل تفتح اللي محتاجه بس وقت المذاكرة أو المراجعة السريعة، بدل ما تفتح صفحة واحدة ضخمة. 📂 الفهرس 1️⃣ الأساسيات: Window Functions, OVER, PARTITION BY, ORDER BY المفهوم الأساسي، الفرق مع GROUP BY، الشكل العام للـ OVER()، وترتيب ORDER BY جوه وبره OVER. 2️⃣ Ranking Functions: ROW\ NUMBER, RANK, DENSE\ RANK, NTILE مقارنة الثلاث دوال الترقيم، Tie-breaking، وNTILE للـ paging والـ bucketing (quartiles/deciles). 3️⃣ Fetching Functions: LAG, LEAD, FIRST\ VALUE, LAST\ VALUE الصف السابق/التالي، أول/آخر قيمة، وأهم فخ في LAST\ VALUE مع الـ default frame. 4️⃣ Aggregate Functions & Window Frames: Running/Moving Totals SUM/AVG/MAX كـ window functions، Window Frames بالتفصيل، ROWS vs RANGE، والـ Moving Average/Total. 5️⃣ أمثلة تطبيقية مركّبة (CTE + Patterns) CTE مع window functions، وأشهر الأنماط الجاهزة زي "Top 3 per group". 6️⃣ Paging & Pivoting تقسيم النتائج لصفحات بـ ROW\ NUMBER، وتحويل الـ Rows لـ Columns (Pivot / CROSSTAB). 7️⃣ GROUP BY Extensions: ROLLUP, CUBE, COALESCE, STRING\ AGG Subtotals والـ Grand Total، الفرق بين ROLLUP وCUBE، وتنظيف النتائج بـ COALESCE وSTRING\ AGG. 8️⃣ Cheat Sheets, Exam Traps & Execution Order كل الـ Cheat Sheets وDecision Guides، أشهر 11 فخ في الامتحانات، وترتيب تنفيذ الـ SQL query. ⭐ الخلاصة النهائية (Golden Rule) OVER() ↓ Window Function PARTITION BY ↓ مين في نفس المجموعة؟ ORDER BY ↓ ما ترتيبهم؟ ROWS / RANGE ↓ أي صفوف تدخل في الحساب؟ FUNCTION ↓ ماذا أريد أن أحسب؟ قاعدة ذهبية: PARTITION BY يحدد مين مع مين ، ORDER BY يحدد مين قبل مين ، والـ FRAME يحدد أي صفوف تدخل الحساب . Window Functions تعمل عبر عدة صفوف مرتبطة بالـ current row، لكنها لا تختزل الصفوف مثل GROUP BY .

title: 1. الأنواع الرئيسية في PostgreSQL
text: 📅 10 — Date & Time Analytics — Complete Reference Define time buckets, missing periods and independent event sequences. 1. الأنواع الرئيسية في PostgreSQL الـTimestamps ممكن تحتوي على أجزاء من الثانية لحد الـmicroseconds. 1.2 ISO 8601 قيم التاريخ/الوقت في PostgreSQL بتتمثل غالبًا بصيغة واضحة تبدأ بالسنة زي: 2018-01-10 13:00:00 الترتيب: year → month → day → hour → minute → second المكونات الأصغر بتستخدم أصفار بادئة (leading zeros) عند الحاجة. 1.3 المناطق الزمنية (Time Zones) و UTC الـtimestamp ممكن يتمثل مع معلومة المنطقة الزمنية. المنطقة الزمنية بتتعبّر كـoffset من UTC، مثال: 2018-01-10 13:00:00+02 لازم تفرّق بين: التعامل مع الـtimezone مهم جدًا للتطبيقات العالمية، سجلات الأحداث (event logs)، والتقارير عبر مناطق مختلفة. 1.4 مقارنة التواريخ والـTimestamps التواريخ/الـtimestamps ممكن تتقارن باستخدام: = = مثال: SELECT FROM orders WHERE order date = '2026-01-01'; الـtimestamp الحالي: SELECT NOW(); 1.5 طرح التواريخ (Date Subtraction) طرح تاريخين/timestamps بينتج مدة ( INTERVAL ): SELECT end time - start time AS duration FROM events; ده مفيد لـ: 1.6 إضافة تواريخ وIntervals إضافة integer لـ DATE بتضيف أيام: SELECT DATE '2026-01-10' + 7; لوحدات زمنية أكبر، استخدم interval: SELECT DATE '2026-01-10' + INTERVAL '1 year'; تقدر تجمع أكتر من وحدة مع بعض: SELECT TIMESTAMP '2026-01-10 10:00:00' + INTERVAL '1 year 2 days 3 minutes'; فخ: إضافة integer لـtimestamp مش زي إضافته لـdate؛ استخدم INTERVAL لأي عملية حسابية على timestamp.

title: 2. استخراج وتقريب مكونات التاريخ/الوقت
text: 📅 10 — Date & Time Analytics — Complete Reference Define time buckets, missing periods and independent event sequences. 2. استخراج وتقريب مكونات التاريخ/الوقت 2.1 EXTRACT و DATE\ PART أشهر الحقول: مثال: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order date) AS year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM order date) AS month FROM orders; نفس الفكرة بصيغة DATE PART : SELECT DATE PART('year', order date) AS year, DATE PART('month', order date) AS month FROM orders; EXTRACT و DATE PART بيقدموا نفس العملية المفاهيمية بصياغة مختلفة. تذكير بخصوص DOW في PostgreSQL، DOW بتستخدم: Sunday = 0 Monday = 1 ... Saturday = 6 نصيحة: الحقول الزمنية اللي مش متعود عليها ممكن يكون لها تعريف غير متوقع. راجع توثيق PostgreSQL قبل ما تبني عليها أي business logic. 2.2 التجميع حسب مكوّن تاريخ مثال: قارن المبيعات شهريًا عبر عدة سنوات. SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale date) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total sales FROM sales GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM sale date) ORDER BY month; ده بيجاوب على أسئلة زي: هل مبيعات يناير عادةً أعلى من مبيعات مارس؟ 2.3 DATE\ TRUNC DATE TRUNC بتحتفظ بمستوى دقة معين وبتصفّر المكونات الأصغر. SELECT DATE TRUNC('month', TIMESTAMP '2019-07-15 14:35:22'); -- 2019-07-01 00:00:00 النموذج الذهني: 2019-07-15 14:35:22 ↓ DATE TRUNC('month') 2019-07-01 00:00:00 استخدمها لما تحتاج تجمع timestamps في time buckets أكبر: SELECT DATE TRUNC('month', sale time) AS month, SUM(amount) AS total sales FROM sales GROUP BY DATE TRUNC('month', sale time) ORDER BY month; EXTRACT مقابل DATE\ TRUNC قاعدة القرار: لو محتاج المكوّن الرقمي نفسه، استخدم EXTRACT . لو محتاج time bucket يتم تجميعه/دمجه كـdate-like value، DATE TRUNC غالبًا أفيد.

title: 3. GENERATE\ SERIES مع التاريخ/الوقت
text: 📅 10 — Date & Time Analytics — Complete Reference Define time buckets, missing periods and independent event sequences. 3. GENERATE\ SERIES مع التاريخ/الوقت 3.1 النمط الأساسي GENERATE SERIES تقدر تولّد بيها سلسلة من الـtimestamps. SELECT FROM GENERATE SERIES( '2026-01-01'::timestamp, '2026-01-05'::timestamp, INTERVAL '1 day' ) AS t(day); القيم المولّدة بتستمر طالما القيمة التالية أصغر من أو تساوي قيمة النهاية. تقدر تستخدم ساعات كمان: SELECT FROM GENERATE SERIES( '2026-01-01 09:00'::timestamp, '2026-01-01 14:00'::timestamp, INTERVAL '1 hour' ) AS t(hour); 3.2 ليه نولّد من بداية الفترة؟ تجنب توليد سلسلة شهرية بدءًا من يوم 31. إضافة شهر لـ31 يناير ممكن توديك لـ28 فبراير، وبعدين إضافة شهر تاني هتديك 28 مارس مش 31. النمط الآمن: SELECT month start FROM GENERATE SERIES( '2026-01-01'::date, '2026-12-01'::date, INTERVAL '1 month' ) AS s(month start); عشان تجيب آخر يوم في كل شهر: SELECT month start + INTERVAL '1 month' - INTERVAL '1 day' AS month end FROM GENERATE SERIES( '2026-01-01'::date, '2026-12-01'::date, INTERVAL '1 month' ) AS s(month start); قاعدة: ولّد من بدايات فترات ثابتة، واشتق نهايات الفترات بعد كده. 3.3 اكتشاف الفترات الزمنية المفقودة الـaggregation العادي بيرجع بس الفترات اللي فعلًا موجودة في البيانات. مثال للمشكلة: 09:00 → 5 sales 10:00 → 3 sales 12:00 → 4 sales الساعة 11:00 مش ظاهرة، رغم إنها كانت فعلًا صفر مبيعات. اعمل سلسلة كاملة واعمل LEFT JOIN مع البيانات: WITH hour series AS ( SELECT hour FROM GENERATE SERIES( '2026-01-01 09:00'::timestamp, '2026-01-01 14:00'::timestamp, INTERVAL '1 hour' ) AS s(hour) ) SELECT h.hour, COUNT(s.sale time) AS sales count FROM hour series h LEFT JOIN sales s ON DATE TRUNC('hour', s.sale time) = h.hour GROUP BY h.hour ORDER BY h.hour; مهم: عد عمود الحدث القابل لـNULL ( COUNT(s.sale time) )، مش COUNT( ) ، عشان الفترات المفقودة تبقى صفر بدل واحد.

title: 4. فترات زمنية مخصصة (Time Bins / Intervals)
text: 📅 10 — Date & Time Analytics — Complete Reference Define time buckets, missing periods and independent event sequences. 4. فترات زمنية مخصصة (Time Bins / Intervals) لما الـbucket المطلوب مش حقل تاريخ طبيعي، اعمل bins واضحة. مثال: فترات مبيعات كل 3 ساعات. WITH bins AS ( SELECT lower bound, lower bound + INTERVAL '3 hours' AS upper bound FROM GENERATE SERIES( '2026-01-01 09:00'::timestamp, '2026-01-01 15:00'::timestamp, INTERVAL '3 hours' ) AS s(lower bound) ) SELECT b.lower bound, b.upper bound, COUNT(s.sale time) AS sales count FROM bins b LEFT JOIN sales s ON s.sale time = b.lower bound AND s.sale time < b.upper bound GROUP BY b.lower bound, b.upper bound ORDER BY b.lower bound; الفترة نصف المفتوحة (half-open interval): lower bound <= time < upper bound بتمنع القيم على الحد الفاصل من إنها تتحسب في bin-ين.

title: 5. LAG / LEAD لحساب الوقت بين الأحداث
text: 📅 10 — Date & Time Analytics — Complete Reference Define time buckets, missing periods and independent event sequences. 5. LAG / LEAD لحساب الوقت بين الأحداث 5.1 المشكلة الأساسية تخيل عمود فيه كل أوقات الأحداث: 09:07 09:13 09:40 10:20 السؤال: كام وقت بيعدي بين الأحداث المتتالية؟ محتاج تجيب قيمة الصف السابق أو التالي. 5.2 LAG LAG(column) بترجع قيمة من صف سابق داخل window مرتبة. SELECT sale time, LAG(sale time) OVER ( ORDER BY sale time ) AS previous sale FROM sales; النتيجة من الناحية المفاهيمية: 5.3 الوقت منذ الحدث السابق SELECT sale time, sale time - LAG(sale time) OVER ( ORDER BY sale time ) AS time since previous FROM sales; الصف الأول بيكون NULL لأنه معندوش حدث سابق. 5.4 LEAD LEAD(column) بترجع قيمة من الصف التالي. SELECT sale time, LEAD(sale time) OVER ( ORDER BY sale time ) AS next sale FROM sales; مقارنة سريعة 5.5 الإزاحة (Offset) الافتراضي هو 1: LAG(value) صفين للخلف: LAG(value, 2) صفين للقدام: LEAD(value, 2) 5.6 متوسط الوقت بين الأحداث متعملش nest لـwindow function جوه aggregate على نفس مستوى الـquery: -- ❌ متستخدمش هذا النمط AVG(sale time - LAG(sale time) OVER (...)) بدل من كده استخدم مرحلتين منطقيتين: SELECT AVG(time between) FROM ( SELECT sale time - LAG(sale time) OVER ( ORDER BY sale time ) AS time between FROM sales ) AS gaps; النموذج الذهني: Events ↓ LAG() ↓ Time between events ↓ Subquery / CTE ↓ AVG() 5.7 LAG لتغيّر السلسلة الزمنية LAG/LEAD مش مقتصرة على الـtimestamps. مثال: SELECT sale date, sales, sales - LAG(sales) OVER ( ORDER BY sale date ) AS change from previous FROM daily sales; ده بيدّيك: current value - previous value لحساب النسبة المئوية للتغيّر: (current - previous) / previous × 100 التطبيق القوي غالبًا بيحسب القيمة السابقة مرة واحدة في CTE/subquery وبعدين يستخدمها في الخطوة اللي بعدها. 5.8 PARTITION BY مع LAG/LEAD لو فيه كيانات مستقلة متعددة، اعمل partition للـwindow. مثال: الوقت بين الأحداث لكل عميل : SELECT customer id, event time, LAG(event time) OVER ( PARTITION BY customer id ORDER BY event time ) AS previous event FROM customer events; النموذج الذهني: PARTITION BY → مين مع مين؟ ORDER BY → مين قبل مين؟ LAG/LEAD → أجيب قيمة منين؟ من غير PARTITION BY ، ممكن يتقارن حدث عميل بحدث عميل تاني بالغلط. لمرجع أشمل عن Window Functions يغطي الـranking، الـframes، FIRST VALUE ، LAST VALUE ، ROLLUP ، CUBE ، وأكتر، راجع مرجع SQL Window Functions — Complete Reference Guide المربوط بالفعل في هذه المكتبة.

text: 🔤 11 — Text, String & Pattern Matching — Complete Reference Clean and classify text without confusing NULL, empty strings and spaces. 1.13 نمط جدول إعادة الترميز (Recoding Table) لما يكون فيه قيم فوضوية كتير أو محتاج mappings صريحة، جدول مؤقت لإعادة الترميز غالبًا بيكون أوضح من CASE ضخمة. الخطوة 1 — إنشاء جدول الـmapping CREATE TEMP TABLE fruit recode AS SELECT DISTINCT fav fruit AS original, fav fruit AS standardized FROM survey; الخطوة 2 — تحديث القيم الموحّدة UPDATE fruit recode SET standardized = LOWER(TRIM(original)); تصحيحات إضافية مستهدفة ممكن تستخدم WHERE : UPDATE fruit recode SET standardized = 'banana' WHERE original LIKE '%nn%'; الخطوة 3 — ربط الـmapping بالبيانات الأصلية SELECT r.standardized, COUNT( ) AS n FROM survey s JOIN fruit recode r ON s.fav fruit = r.original GROUP BY r.standardized ORDER BY n DESC; متى تفضّل أسلوب جدول الـmapping: استثناءات صريحة كتير، mappings قابلة لإعادة الاستخدام، منطق تنظيف قابل للتدقيق (auditable)، أو محتاج تفصل القيم الخام عن القيم الموحّدة.

title: 8. الحالة المتكاملة الختامية — قرار استثمار MovieNow
text: 📊 12 — Analytical SQL Patterns — Comprehensive Reference Translate the MovieNow business question into a grain-safe analytical query. 8. الحالة المتكاملة الختامية — قرار استثمار MovieNow هل العملاء بيدّوا تقييمات أحسن للأفلام الأحدث، وهل النمط بيختلف حسب دولة العميل؟ السياق MovieNow بتفكر تستثمر في أفلام جديدة، والأفلام الحديثة أغلى في الإضافة، فالإدارة عايزة دليل إن العملاء فعلًا بيقيّموا الإصدارات الجديدة بشكل أحسن. الخطوات WHERE r.movie id IN ( SELECT movie id FROM renting GROUP BY movie id HAVING COUNT(rating) = 4 ) AND r.rental date = '2018-04-01' الاستعلام الكامل SELECT m.release year, c.country, COUNT( ) AS n rentals, COUNT(DISTINCT m.movie id) AS n movies, AVG(r.rating) AS avg rating FROM renting AS r JOIN customers AS c ON r.customer id = c.customer id JOIN movies AS m ON r.movie id = m.movie id WHERE r.movie id IN ( SELECT movie id FROM renting GROUP BY movie id HAVING COUNT(rating) = 4 ) AND r.rental date = '2018-04-01' GROUP BY ROLLUP (m.release year, c.country) ORDER BY c.country, m.release year; تفسير النتيجة في نتيجة الدرس: 333 إيجار، 50 فيلم مختلف، متوسط تقييم 7.9 ، ومفيش نمط واضح إن الأفلام الأحدث بتاخد تقييمات أعلى. استنتاج بيزنس مقابل استنتاج إحصائي النتيجة الوصفية بتقول مفيش اتجاه واضح، لكن ده مش دليل قاطع إن سنة الإصدار معندهاش تأثير. استنتاج أقوى محتاج تحليل إحصائي حقيقي (حجم العينة، التباين، confidence intervals، hypothesis testing، أو انحدار/ارتباط مناسب). SQL بيوصلك لحد وصف البيانات، مش لحد الإثبات الإحصائي.

title: 2. ما هو CASE؟
text: 🅰️ CASE Statements — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 2. ما هو CASE؟ CASE هو الطريقة الأساسية في SQL لعمل منطق شبيه بـ IF / ELSE IF / ELSE . CASE WHEN condition 1 THEN result 1 WHEN condition 2 THEN result 2 ELSE result else END AS alias المكونات: WHEN يختبر condition، THEN النتيجة إذا True، ELSE النتيجة إذا لم يتحقق أي WHEN، END نهاية الـ CASE، AS alias اسم الـ output column. Mental model: WHEN condition? ├── TRUE → THEN result └── FALSE → next WHEN └── لا يوجد True → ELSE 2.1 مثال: نتيجة مباراة SELECT home goal, away goal, CASE WHEN home goal away goal THEN 'Home win' WHEN home goal < away goal THEN 'Away win' ELSE 'Tie' END AS outcome FROM match; 2.2 CASE مع أكثر من شرط يمكن استخدام AND و OR داخل WHEN . مثال: هل Chelsea فاز؟ SELECT home team id, away team id, home goal, away goal, CASE WHEN home team id = 8455 AND home goal away goal THEN 'Chelsea home win!' WHEN away team id = 8455 AND away goal home goal THEN 'Chelsea away win!' ELSE 'Loss or tie :(' END AS chelsea result FROM match WHERE home team id = 8455 OR away team id = 8455; لماذا الـ WHERE مهم هنا؟ بدونه، ELSE 'Loss or tie :(' لن تعني بالضرورة أن Chelsea خسر أو تعادل؛ بل ستشمل أي مباراة لا تحقق الشرطين ، حتى مباريات لا يلعب فيها Chelsea أصلًا. قاعدة مهمة: معنى ELSE يعتمد على الـ population التي وصلت إلى CASE. راجع دائمًا ما الذي يدخل الـ CASE أصلًا.

title: 4. CASE + Aggregate Functions
text: 🅰️ CASE Statements — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 4. CASE + Aggregate Functions من أهم أفكار Intermediate SQL — يمكن وضع CASE داخل COUNT , SUM , و AVG لعمل conditional aggregation . 4.1 CASE داخل COUNT السؤال: كم مباراة فاز بها Liverpool على أرضه وخارج أرضه في كل Season؟ SELECT season, COUNT( CASE WHEN hometeam id = AND home goal away goal THEN id END ) AS home wins, COUNT( CASE WHEN awayteam id = AND away goal home goal THEN id END ) AS away wins FROM match GROUP BY season; CASE condition TRUE → returns id condition FALSE → returns NULL COUNT(id/NULL) → counts only non-NULL results 4.2 CASE داخل SUM SELECT season, SUM( CASE WHEN hometeam id = THEN home goal WHEN awayteam id = THEN away goal ELSE 0 END ) AS liverpool goals FROM match GROUP BY season; COUNT(CASE...) = كم Row يحقق الشرط؟ \ SUM(CASE...) = ما مجموع القيم للـ Rows التي تحقق الشرط؟ 4.3 CASE داخل AVG SELECT season, AVG( CASE WHEN hometeam id = THEN home goal WHEN awayteam id = THEN away goal END ) AS avg liverpool goals FROM match GROUP BY season; بدون ELSE ، الحالات غير المتعلقة بـ Liverpool تصبح NULL ، و AVG يتجاهل NULL. هذا غالبًا أفضل من ELSE 0 إذا كان المطلوب متوسط مباريات Liverpool فقط؛ لأن ELSE 0 سيضيف أصفارًا لمباريات لا تخص Liverpool ويشوّه المتوسط.

title: 6. Percentages باستخدام CASE + AVG
text: 🅰️ CASE Statements — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 6. Percentages باستخدام CASE + AVG السؤال: ما نسبة مباريات Liverpool التي فاز بها في كل Season؟ SELECT season, ROUND( 100.0 AVG( CASE WHEN hometeam id = AND home goal away goal THEN 1 WHEN awayteam id = AND away goal home goal THEN 1 WHEN hometeam id = OR awayteam id = THEN 0 END ), 2 ) AS win percentage FROM match GROUP BY season; لماذا هذه الطريقة تعمل؟ Win → 1 Loss → 0 Tie → 0 Not Liverpool → NULL AVG(1, 0, 1, 1, 0) = 3/5 = 0.60 = 60% المبدأ: Percentage = average of a 0/1 indicator تحذير شديد الأهمية لا تجعل مباريات لا تخص Liverpool تساوي 0 إذا كنت تريد نسبة انتصارات Liverpool؛ يجب أن تكون NULL حتى لا تدخل denominator.

title: 8. Common Mistakes
text: 🅰️ CASE Statements — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 8. Common Mistakes Mistake 1 — ELSE خاطئة منطقيًا CASE WHEN chelsea home win THEN 'Chelsea win' WHEN chelsea away win THEN 'Chelsea win' ELSE 'Chelsea loss' END لو لم تحدد WHERE أن Chelsea لعبت، فالـ ELSE تشمل مباريات لا تخص Chelsea. Fix: filter population أو استخدم CASE أكثر دقة. Mistake 2 — إدخال غير المهتمين كـ 0 في percentage خطأ: AVG( CASE WHEN liverpool win THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ) إذا كان dataset يحتوي مباريات لا تخص Liverpool، فهي ستدخل denominator. أفضل: AVG( CASE WHEN liverpool win THEN 1 WHEN liverpool loss or tie THEN 0 ELSE NULL END )

title: 4. Subquery في FROM — Derived Table
text: 🔍 Simple Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 4. Subquery في FROM — Derived Table 4.1 الفكرة أحيانًا تحتاج أولًا أن تحسب aggregate لكل Group، ثم تعمل aggregate آخر على نتائج الـ aggregate الأول. مثال: احسب متوسط home goals لكل فريق في موسم 2011/2012، ثم اعرض أعلى 3 فرق. SELECT team, home avg FROM ( SELECT t.team long name AS team, AVG(m.home goal) AS home avg FROM team AS t LEFT JOIN match AS m ON t.team api id = m.hometeam id WHERE m.season = '2011/2012' GROUP BY t.team long name ) AS team stats ORDER BY home avg DESC LIMIT 3; الـ Subquery أصبحت كأنها Table اسمها team stats . القاعدة: FROM subquery = Derived Table / intermediate dataset. 4.2 لماذا الـ alias ضروري؟ في كثير من SQL dialects، الـ derived table في FROM تحتاج alias: FROM ( SELECT ... ) AS team stats 4.3 أكثر من Subquery في FROM FROM ( SELECT ... ) AS a JOIN ( SELECT ... ) AS b ON a.key = b.key شرط مهم: يجب أن يكون لديك Columns مناسبة لعمل الـ JOIN.

title: 7. Filter Scope — أهم مصدر للأخطاء
text: 🔍 Simple Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 7. Filter Scope — أهم مصدر للأخطاء كل Simple Subquery مستقلة منطقيًا عن الـ Outer Query. لا تفترض أن WHERE في الـ Main Query تنتقل تلقائيًا إلى الـ Subquery. SELECT home goal, ( SELECT AVG(home goal) FROM match ) AS overall avg FROM match WHERE season = '2013/2014'; Outer Query → 2013/2014 فقط Subquery → كل Seasons إذا كان المطلوب هو متوسط 2013/2014، يجب أن يكون الـ filter داخل الـ Subquery أيضًا: SELECT home goal, ( SELECT AVG(home goal) FROM match WHERE season = '2013/2014' ) AS season avg FROM match WHERE season = '2013/2014'; قاعدة Population: قبل أي aggregate اسأل: "أنا بحسب الـ average/count على أنهي Population بالضبط؟" ثم تأكد أن Filters تعكس هذه الـ Population.

title: 1. ما هي Correlated Subquery؟
text: 🔗 Correlated Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 1. ما هي Correlated Subquery؟ الـ Correlated Subquery هي Subquery تعتمد على قيمة أو أكثر من الـ outer query لكي تنتج نتيجتها. بعكس الـ simple subquery، لا يمكن عادةً تنفيذها بمفردها؛ لأنها تشير إلى Column من نطاق الـ outer query. Mental model: Outer Query → يختار Row ↓ Correlated Subquery → تستخدم قيمة من هذا الـ Row ↓ تحسب نتيجة تخص هذا الـ Row ↓ Outer Query → ينتقل للـ Row التالي، وتُقيّم الـ subquery مرة أخرى Core idea: الـ subquery ليست مستقلة؛ هي "مرتبطة" بالـ current row/group في الـ outer query.

Correlated Subquery مع EXISTS SELECT c.customer id, c.customer name FROM customers AS c WHERE EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM orders AS o WHERE o.customer id = c.customer id ); المعنى: أعطني العملاء الذين لديهم طلب واحد على الأقل. EXISTS ├── توجد Row مطابقة → TRUE └── لا توجد Row → FALSE Tip: عندما يكون السؤال بصيغة "هل يوجد؟ / على الأقل واحد؟" فكر مباشرةً في EXISTS . لا نهتم بالقيمة المُرجَعة، لذلك نكتب SELECT 1 .

title: 8. Performance
text: 🔗 Correlated Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 8. title: 9. Correlated Subquery vs Window Functions
text: 🔗 Correlated Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 9. Correlated Subquery vs Window Functions مثال: الموظفون الذين راتبهم أعلى من متوسط قسمهم. Correlated subquery: SELECT e.employee id, e.department id, e.salary FROM employees AS e WHERE e.salary ( SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM employees AS e2 WHERE e2.department id = e.department id ); Window-function approach: SELECT employee id, department id, salary FROM ( SELECT employee id, department id, salary, AVG(salary) OVER ( PARTITION BY department id ) AS department avg salary FROM employees ) AS x WHERE salary department avg salary; Advanced tip: إذا كان المطلوب "قيمة aggregate بجانب كل Row" فكر في window functions أيضًا، وليس فقط correlated subqueries.

title: 1. ما هي Nested Subqueries؟
text: 🪆 Nested Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 1. ما هي Nested Subqueries؟ الـ Nested Subquery هي Subquery موجودة داخل Subquery أخرى: Main Query ↓ Outer Subquery ↓ Inner Subquery بعض الأسئلة تحتاج أكثر من مرحلة transformation/aggregation/filtering قبل الوصول إلى النتيجة النهائية. Mental model: كل مستوى يحل جزءًا من المشكلة، ثم يسلّم الـ intermediate result إلى المستوى الذي يليه. 1.1 لماذا نحتاجها؟ مثال السؤال: كيف يختلف إجمالي الأهداف في كل شهر عن متوسط إجمالي الأهداف الشهري؟ 1. احسب total goals لكل شهر ↓ 2. احسب AVG لهذه النتائج الشهرية ↓ 3. قارن total goals لكل شهر بالـ average

title: 3. مثال كامل — Monthly Goals vs Monthly Average
text: 🪆 Nested Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 3. مثال كامل — Monthly Goals vs Monthly Average السؤال: How does each month's total goals differ from the monthly average of goals scored؟ 3.1 المستوى الأول — Inner Subquery SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month, SUM(home goal + away goal) AS monthly goals FROM match GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) الناتج أصبح one row per month بدلًا من one row per match. 3.2 المستوى الثاني — Outer Subquery SELECT AVG(monthly goals) AS avg monthly goals FROM ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month, SUM(home goal + away goal) AS monthly goals FROM match GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) ) AS monthly; الناتج هنا Scalar Value واحدة — الـ subquery داخل FROM أنشأت Derived Table، ثم الـ outer level عملت AVG عليها. 3.3 المستوى الثالث — Main Query SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month, SUM(home goal + away goal) AS monthly goals, SUM(home goal + away goal) - ( SELECT AVG(monthly goals) FROM ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month, SUM(home goal + away goal) AS monthly goals FROM match GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) ) AS monthly ) AS difference FROM match GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) ORDER BY month; Main Query ├── احسب monthly goals لكل شهر └── Subquery └── Outer Subquery └── Inner Subquery → احسب monthly goals لكل شهر → AVG(monthly goals) → average monthly goals → monthly goals - average إذا كانت Difference موجبة → الشهر أعلى من المتوسط، سالبة → أقل، صفر → يساوي المتوسط.

title: 4. Nested ≠ Correlated
text: 🪆 Nested Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 4. Nested ≠ Correlated Nested تصف الـ structure/depth ، بينما Correlated تصف الـ dependency . يمكن أن تكون Nested Subquery: nested+uncorrelated، nested+correlated، أو فيها أكثر من مستوى وبعض المستويات correlated وبعضها لا. Nested Uncorrelated: Main Query → Outer Subquery → Inner Subquery (بلا reference لمستوى خارجي) Nested Correlated: Main Query → Outer Subquery ← correlated with Main Query → Inner Subquery Golden distinction: \- Nested = أين توجد الـ subquery؟ داخل subquery أخرى. \- Correlated = هل تعتمد على قيمة من outer query؟

title: 5. Correlated Nested Subqueries
text: 🪆 Nested Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 5. Correlated Nested Subqueries مثال السؤال: ما متوسط الأهداف لكل دولة في موسم 2011/2012؟ SELECT c.name AS country, ( SELECT AVG(total goals) FROM ( SELECT m.home goal + m.away goal AS total goals FROM match AS m WHERE m.country id = c.id AND m.season = '2011/2012' ) AS country matches ) AS avg goals FROM country AS c; أين الـ Correlation؟ في WHERE m.country id = c.id — c.id يأتي من Main Query. أين الـ Nesting؟ Main Query → Outer Scalar Subquery → Inner Derived-Table Subquery Important: الـ correlation لا يلزم أن تكون مع الـ Main Query مباشرة؛ يمكن أن ترتبط الـ inner subquery بمستوى خارجي آخر حسب الـ SQL dialect.

title: 8. Nested Subquery vs CTE
text: 🪆 Nested Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 8. Nested Subquery vs CTE Nested form: SELECT AVG(monthly goals) FROM ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month, SUM(home goal + away goal) AS monthly goals FROM match GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) ) AS monthly; CTE form: WITH monthly AS ( SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month, SUM(home goal + away goal) AS monthly goals FROM match GROUP BY EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) ) SELECT AVG(monthly goals) AS avg monthly goals FROM monthly; Tip: إذا أصبحت الـ nesting عميقة جدًا، فكر في CTEs لتحسين readability وmaintainability.

title: 9. Nested Subquery vs Window Function
text: 🪆 Nested Subqueries — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 9. title: 1. ما هو الـ CTE؟
text: 🧩 Common Table Expressions (CTEs) — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 1. ما هو الـ CTE؟ Common Table Expression (CTE) هو طريقة لتعريف intermediate result في بداية الـ SQL statement باستخدام WITH ، ثم التعامل معه بالاسم داخل الـ main query كما لو كان table مؤقتًا ضمن نطاق الاستعلام. WITH cte name AS ( SELECT ... FROM ... ) SELECT ... FROM cte name; Mental model: WITH → عرّف intermediate dataset باسم → Main Query → استخدم الاسم كأنه table Core idea: الـ CTE لا يغير منطق الـ query؛ هو غالبًا يعيد تنظيمه إلى named, readable steps.

title: 2. لماذا نستخدم CTE؟
text: 🧩 Common Table Expressions (CTEs) — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 2. لماذا نستخدم CTE؟ عندما تصبح الـ subqueries طويلة ومتداخلة، يصعب الإجابة عن: ما الذي تفعله كل Subquery؟ لماذا نحتاجها؟ ما شكل الـ intermediate result؟ هل هناك transformation غير ضرورية؟ بدلًا من: Main Query → Subquery → Subquery → Subquery يمكن كتابة: CTE 1 → CTE 2 → CTE 3 → Main Query وهذا غالبًا يجعل الـ SQL أسهل في القراءة والـ debugging والـ maintenance.

title: 3. تحويل Subquery داخل FROM إلى CTE
text: 🧩 Common Table Expressions (CTEs) — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 3. تحويل Subquery داخل FROM إلى CTE بالـ Subquery: SELECT c.name AS country, COUNT(s.id) AS matches FROM country AS c JOIN ( SELECT country id, id FROM match WHERE home goal + away goal = 10 ) AS s ON c.id = s.country id GROUP BY c.name; بالـ CTE: WITH s AS ( SELECT country id, id FROM match WHERE home goal + away goal = 10 ) SELECT c.name AS country, COUNT(s.id) AS matches FROM country AS c JOIN s ON c.id = s.country id GROUP BY c.name; النتيجة المنطقية نفسها؛ الفرق الأساسي في organization/readability. Tip: أعطِ الـ CTE اسمًا يصف محتواه بدلًا من أسماء غامضة مثل s , x , tmp1 عندما يكون الاستعلام كبيرًا. مثال أفضل: WITH high scoring matches AS (...) .

title: 6. تصحيح مفهوم مهم عن Performance
text: 🧩 Common Table Expressions (CTEs) — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 6. تصحيح مفهوم مهم عن Performance قد تسمع: "CTE تُنفذ مرة واحدة ثم تُخزن في memory، ولذلك هي أسرع." هذه ليست قاعدة عامة . الـ CTE هي أساسًا query construct لتنظيم الاستعلام. طريقة تنفيذها — وهل يتم materialize أم inline — تعتمد على الـ database engine والإصدار والـ query plan. CTE ≠ automatically faster Subquery ≠ automatically slower في PostgreSQL مثلًا، بعض CTEs يمكن للـ optimizer دمجها داخل الـ parent query، بينما قد يحدث materialization في حالات أخرى أو عند استخدام MATERIALIZED . Golden performance rule: لا تختار CTE بدل Subquery لمجرد توقع أنها أسرع. اخترها أولًا للوضوح، ثم استخدم EXPLAIN عندما يكون الأداء مهمًا.

title: 2. مقارنة عامة
text: 🎯 Choosing the Right SQL Technique + Final Case Study Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 2. مقارنة عامة 2.1 JOIN SELECT c.name, m.id, m.home goal, m.away goal FROM country AS c JOIN match AS m ON m.country id = c.id; فكر في JOIN عندما تقول: "أريد بيانات من الجدول A مع بيانات من الجدول B." الـ JOIN ممتاز عندما تكون relationship بين datasets هي قلب الـ query. 2.2 متى يكون Correlated Subquery مفيدًا؟ SELECT e.employee id, e.salary FROM employees AS e WHERE e.salary ( SELECT AVG(e2.salary) FROM employees AS e2 WHERE e2.department id = e.department id ); Performance note: لا تحفظ أن correlated subquery "دائمًا بطيئة". قد تكون مكلفة، لكن الـ optimizer قد يعيد صياغتها. استخدم execution plan للقرار النهائي. 2.3 متى أستخدم Multiple/Nested Subqueries؟ عندما تحتاج عدة transformations متتابعة قبل أن تصبح البيانات بالشكل المطلوب، مثلًا: Filter → Group → Calculate → Aggregate. Key idea: Nested Subqueries مناسبة عندما يكون هناك multi-step transformation، وليس لأنها "أفضل" من CTE بالضرورة. 2.4 متى أستخدم CTE؟ WITH filtered sales AS ( SELECT FROM sales WHERE sale date = DATE '2026-01-01' ), rep totals AS ( SELECT sales rep id, SUM(amount) AS total sales FROM filtered sales GROUP BY sales rep id ), ranked reps AS ( SELECT sales rep id, total sales, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total sales DESC) AS rnk FROM rep totals ) SELECT FROM ranked reps WHERE rnk <= 10; filtered sales → rep totals → ranked reps → Top 10 CTE ممتازة أيضًا عندما: تريد أسماء واضحة للـ intermediate datasets، تريد تقسيم business logic إلى خطوات، تحتاج أكثر من CTE في نفس statement، تريد تقليل nesting depth، أو تحتاج Recursive CTE لاحقًا.

title: 9. Final Case Study — Who Defeated Manchester United?
text: 🎯 Choosing the Right SQL Technique + Final Case Study Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 9. Final Case Study — Who Defeated Manchester United? السؤال النهائي: Who defeated Manchester United in the 2013/2014 season? هذا السؤال يجمع عدة concepts: 9.1 لماذا هذا Case Study جيد؟ المشكلة المهمة هنا: multiple representations of the same relationship . المباراة تحتوي على home team id / away team id ، بينما جدول الفرق يحتوي على team id / team long name . تحتاج تحويل home team id → home team name و away team id → away team name . مثال ممتاز على مشكلة تحتاج تفكيرًا في query design، وليس مجرد كتابة JOIN بشكل آلي. 9.2 Step 1 — Filter the Relevant Season & Team WHERE season = '2013/2014' AND ( home team id = OR away team id = ) لماذا هذه الخطوة أولًا؟ لأننا لا نريد أن تدخل مباريات غير مرتبطة بالسؤال في الـ calculations اللاحقة. All matches → 2013/2014 → Manchester United matches → Relevant population 9.3 Step 2 — Categorize Match Outcome with CASE CASE WHEN home team id = AND home goal away goal THEN 'Win' WHEN away team id = AND away goal home goal THEN 'Win' WHEN home goal = away goal THEN 'Draw' ELSE 'Loss' END AS outcome لاحظ أن الـ WHERE السابقة ضمنت أن كل row تمثل مباراة Manchester United، لذلك ELSE 'Loss' هنا يمكن تفسيرها بأمان كـ loss. 9.4 Step 3 — Identify Home and Away Team Names match.home team id → teams.team id → home team name match.away team id → teams.team id → away team name يمكن حل ذلك عبر two aliases of the same teams table (self-join pattern): FROM match AS m JOIN teams AS home ON m.home team id = home.team id JOIN teams AS away ON m.away team id = away.team id ثم: home.team long name AS home team, away.team long name AS away team Important: هذه المشكلة ليست مستحيلة باستخدام JOINs من حيث المبدأ؛ CTE ليست الحل الوحيد. استخدام CTEs هنا مفيد لتنظيم الـ logic، لكن ليس لأن JOIN لا يستطيع جلب الفريقين. 9.5 Step 4 — Build a CTE WITH man utd matches AS ( SELECT m.id AS match id, m.date, m.season, home.team long name AS home team, away.team long name AS away team, m.home goal, m.away goal, CASE WHEN m.home team id = AND m.home goal m.away goal THEN 'Win' WHEN m.away team id = AND m.away goal m.home goal THEN 'Win' WHEN m.home goal = m.away goal THEN 'Draw' ELSE 'Loss' END AS outcome FROM match AS m JOIN teams AS home ON m.home team id = home.team id JOIN teams AS away ON m.away team id = away.team id WHERE m.season = '2013/2014' AND ( m.home team id = OR m.away team id = ) ) SELECT FROM man utd matches; 9.6 Step 5 — Calculate Loss Margin إذا كان Manchester United هو home team: away goal - home goal . إذا كان away team: home goal - away goal . يحسب فقط للمباريات الخاسرة: WITH man utd matches AS (...), losses AS ( SELECT , CASE WHEN home team id = THEN away goal - home goal ELSE home goal - away goal END AS loss margin FROM man utd matches WHERE outcome = 'Loss' ) SELECT , RANK() OVER ( ORDER BY loss margin DESC ) AS loss rank FROM losses; لماذا CTE ثانية مفيدة؟ لأنها تفصل: Match identification → Outcome classification → Loss filtering → Loss margin calculation → Ranking. مثال عملي ممتاز على CTE pipeline. 9.7 الـ Query النهائية (Production-Friendly) WITH man utd matches AS ( SELECT m.id AS match id, m.date, m.home team id, m.away team id, home.team long name AS home team, away.team long name AS away team, m.home goal, m.away goal, CASE WHEN m.home team id = AND m.home goal m.away goal THEN 'Win' WHEN m.away team id = AND m.away goal m.home goal THEN 'Win' WHEN m.home goal = m.away goal THEN 'Draw' ELSE 'Loss' END AS outcome FROM match AS m JOIN teams AS home ON m.home team id = home.team id JOIN teams AS away ON m.away team id = away.team id WHERE m.season = '2013/2014' AND ( m.home team id = OR m.away team id = ) ), losses AS ( SELECT , CASE WHEN home team id = THEN away goal - home goal ELSE home goal - away goal END AS loss margin FROM man utd matches WHERE outcome = 'Loss' ) SELECT match id, date, home team, away team, home goal, away goal, loss margin, RANK() OVER ( ORDER BY loss margin DESC ) AS loss rank FROM losses ORDER BY loss rank; Replace everywhere with the actual team ID (e.g. via SELECT team api id FROM team WHERE team long name = 'Manchester United' ). 9.8 What This Case Study Teaches

title: 13. Final Golden Rule
text: 🎯 Choosing the Right SQL Technique + Final Case Study Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 13. Final Golden Rule Don't start with SQL syntax. Start with the business question. 1. What is the population? 2. What is the required grain? 3. What data must be combined? 4. What needs classification? 5. What transformation is required? 6. Do I need to preserve detail rows? 7. What technique expresses the logic most clearly? 8. Does the execution plan meet the performance requirement? 🧠 The Ultimate Intermediate SQL Mental Model BUSINESS QUESTION ↓ REQUIRED GRAIN ↓ ┌──────────┴──────────┐ ↓ ↓ COMBINE DATA TRANSFORM DATA ↓ ↓ JOIN CASE / Subquery / CTE │ │ └──────────┬──────────┘ ↓ ANALYTICAL NEED ↓ ┌─────────────────┼─────────────────┐ ↓ ↓ ↓ GROUP BY WINDOW EXISTS ↓ FUNCTION ↓ Collapse rows Preserve rows Test existence │ │ └────────┬────────┘ ↓ VALIDATE GRAIN ↓ CHECK CORRECTNESS ↓ CHECK EXECUTION PLAN ↓ FINAL RESULT Final takeaway: قوة الـ Intermediate SQL ليست في معرفة عشرات الـ functions منفصلة؛ القوة الحقيقية هي القدرة على تركيبها في pipeline منطقي: Filter → Join → Classify → Transform → Aggregate/Analyze → Rank → Present . 🔗 مراجع ذات صلة Related source

title: 1. إحصائيات وصفية أساسية (Summary Statistics)
text: 📊 Numeric EDA & Statistics — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 1. إحصائيات وصفية أساسية (Summary Statistics) 1.1 Range SELECT MIN(revenue) AS min revenue, MAX(revenue) AS max revenue FROM sales; 1.2 Mean SELECT AVG(revenue) FROM sales; 1.3 Variance SELECT VAR POP(revenue) FROM sales; SELECT VAR SAMP(revenue) FROM sales; في PostgreSQL: VARIANCE() = VAR SAMP() Population vs Sample Population variance: Σ(x - μ)² / N Sample variance: Σ(x - x̄)² / (N - 1) استخدام N - 1 يجعل sample variance عادةً أكبر قليلًا من population variance لنفس البيانات. 1.4 Standard Deviation Standard deviation = square root of variance. STDDEV POP(revenue) STDDEV SAMP(revenue) 1.5 ROUND SELECT ROUND(AVG(revenue), 2) FROM sales; غالبًا اعمل aggregation ثم round للناتج، بدل rounding كل row قبل الـ aggregation، إلا إذا كان business rule يتطلب غير ذلك.

title: 5. Bins مخصصة باستخدام GENERATE\ SERIES

Bins مخصصة باستخدام GENERATE\ SERIES SELECT FROM generate series(0, 100, 20); 5.1 نمط binning حقيقي WITH bins AS ( SELECT generate series(0, 100, 20) AS lower bound, generate series(20, 120, 20) AS upper bound ), eb AS ( SELECT unanswered count FROM stackoverflow WHERE tag = 'amazon-ebs' ) SELECT b.lower bound, b.upper bound, COUNT(e.unanswered count) AS n FROM bins b LEFT JOIN eb e ON e.unanswered count = b.lower bound AND e.unanswered count < b.upper bound GROUP BY b.lower bound, b.upper bound ORDER BY b.lower bound; ليه LEFT JOIN؟ للحفاظ على كل الـ bins حتى لو لم يقع فيها أي observation، وبالتالي COUNT(e.unanswered count) بدل COUNT( ) عشان الـ empty bins تظهر 0 مش تتحذف.

title: 7. Median & Percentiles
text: 📊 Numeric EDA & Statistics — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 7. Median & Percentiles 7.1 Median Median = 50th percentile، مفيد جدًا مع skewed distributions وoutliers لأن mean قد يتأثر بالقيم المتطرفة. 10, 20, 30, 40, 1000 Mean = 220 Median = 30 7.2 Percentile functions PERCENTILE DISC(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) PERCENTILE CONT(0.50) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY salary) DISC ترجع value موجودة فعليًا في البيانات. title: 9. مشاكل شائعة في البيانات الرقمية
text: 📊 Numeric EDA & Statistics — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 9. مشاكل شائعة في البيانات الرقمية 9.1 أكواد خاصة للأخطاء/القيم المفقودة لا تفترض أن 9, 99, -99, 999 قيم حقيقية — قد تعني Unknown/Missing/Not applicable/Refused/Error. Always check the data dictionary/documentation. 9.2 الصفر ممكن ميبقاش صفر فعلي income = 0 ممكن تكون دخل حقيقي = 0، أو missing مُشفّرة كـ0. مش هتعرف من data type لوحده. 9.3 Outliers القيمة المتطرفة مش بالضرورة error — تستاهل investigation مش حذف تلقائي. 9.4 نوع البيانات ≠ المعنى الكمي INTEGER ≠ automatically measurable quantity مثال: ZIP code أو survey response codes — AVG(zip code) أو متوسط department code مالهاش معنى. Data type tells you how data is stored; semantics tell you how data should be analyzed.

title: 10. حالة واقعية — التحقيق في جودة البيانات (GPA)
text: 📊 Numeric EDA & Statistics — Complete Reference Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 10. حالة واقعية — التحقيق في جودة البيانات (GPA) السؤال: "Why is the average student GPA unexpectedly low?" لا تبدأ بـ SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students; مباشرة — ابدأ بالتحقيق: -- Step 1: Coverage SELECT COUNT( ) AS total students, COUNT(gpa) AS students with gpa, COUNT( ) - COUNT(gpa) AS missing gpa FROM students; -- Step 2: Range SELECT MIN(gpa) AS min gpa, MAX(gpa) AS max gpa FROM students; -- Step 3: Distribution SELECT gpa, COUNT( ) AS n FROM students GROUP BY gpa ORDER BY gpa; لو النظام من 0–4 ولقيت MAX = 99 فده red flag. اكتشفت من الـdocumentation إن 99 = Unknown ، فالـaverage الأصلي كان misleading. -- Step 5: Clean analytical population SELECT AVG(gpa) FROM students WHERE gpa BETWEEN 0 AND 4; هذه ليست مجرد SQL syntax exercise؛ هذه data validation before analysis .

title: 1. Core Interview Questions
text: 🎯 🎯 99 — SQL Interview Questions, Traps & Real-World Patterns Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. 1. Core Interview Questions Q0. ما الفرق بين Simple CASE وSearched CASE؟ Simple CASE: بتقارن تعبير واحد بقيم متعددة. Searched CASE: بتقيّم شروط Boolean مستقلة في كل WHEN ... THEN . Q1. What is the difference between a simple, correlated, and nested subquery? Q2. Is every nested subquery correlated? No. Nesting and correlation are different dimensions. A query can be nested but fully uncorrelated. Q3. When would you choose EXISTS instead of IN? عندما يكون السؤال منطقياً: "هل يوجد على الأقل صف مرتبط؟"؛ EXISTS يعبر عن intent بوضوح ولا يحتاج إلى إرجاع قائمة قيم إلى المستوى الخارجي. Q4. CTE vs subquery — what is the difference? CTE غالبًا أوضح للقراءة والتنظيم، خصوصًا عند وجود مراحل متعددة. لكن CTE ليست تلقائيًا أسرع؛ الأداء يعتمد على الـoptimizer والـdialect وخطة التنفيذ. Q5. When is a window function better than a subquery? عندما تريد قيمة محسوبة على مجموعة من الصفوف مع الاحتفاظ بنفس الصفوف التفصيلية، مثل الفرق عن المتوسط أو ranking. Q6. Why can AVG(CASE ... ELSE 0 END) be wrong? لأن الصفوف التي لا تنتمي إلى population المطلوبة تدخل في denominator كأصفار. غالبًا نحتاج NULL للحالات المستبعدة.

title: Pattern Search: LIKE ⭐⭐⭐
text: 🔍 5️⃣ Pattern Matching & Full-Text Search Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. Pattern Search: LIKE ⭐⭐⭐ LIKE يبحث في النص باستخدام wildcards. Wildcards % → zero or more characters → exactly one character أمثلة: -- Starts with ELF SELECT FROM film WHERE title LIKE 'ELF%'; -- Ends with ELF SELECT FROM film WHERE title LIKE '%ELF'; -- Contains ELF SELECT FROM film WHERE title LIKE '%ELF%'; مهم: LIKE case-sensitive في PostgreSQL WHERE title LIKE '%elf%' قد لا تطابق Elf . لو مطلوب case-insensitive matching، PostgreSQL يوفر ILIKE : WHERE title ILIKE '%elf%'; Mental model: LIKE / ILIKE → pattern matching. استخدمه لما تهتم بـ literal character pattern بدل linguistic search.

title: Full-Text Search ⭐⭐⭐
text: 🔍 5️⃣ Pattern Matching & Full-Text Search Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. Full-Text Search ⭐⭐⭐ مصمّم للبحث في natural-language text بشكل أذكى من simple pattern matching. LIKE vs Full-Text Search LIKE ↓ character/pattern matching Full-Text Search ↓ words + normalization + lexemes + linguistic matching أساسيات PostgreSQL full-text search: to tsvector() to tsquery() @@ مثال: SELECT title FROM film WHERE to tsvector('english', title) @@ to tsquery('english', 'elf'); tsvector to tsvector() يحول النص إلى تمثيل قابل للبحث موحّد يحتوي lexemes . SELECT to tsvector('english', 'The quick brown foxes'); Document text ↓ to tsvector() ↓ normalized lexemes tsquery to tsquery() يمثل استعلام المستخدم. SELECT to tsquery('english', 'fox'); ثم المقارنة: tsvector @@ tsquery @@ هو match operator. لماذا Full-Text Search؟ يقدر يراعي linguistic variations عن طريق normalization/stemming وأنسب بكثير من %term% للبحث في natural-language documents. Real use cases: Search product descriptions، knowledge-base articles، support tickets، film/book/article content، database-backed search features. تمييز مهم: Full-text search مش نفس حاجة typo correction. للأخطاء الإملائية وapproximate string similarity، استخدم fuzzy-matching tools مثل levenshtein() أو similarity() (شوف Sub-Note "Extensions & Fuzzy Matching").

title: User-Defined Types & Functions ⭐⭐
text: ⚙️ 7️⃣ Custom Types & Functions Use this supporting source in the context of its canonical SQL module. User-Defined Types & Functions ⭐⭐ PostgreSQL extensible مش بس من خلال extensions، لكن كمان من خلال custom database objects. User-defined data types إنشاء type مخصص بـ CREATE TYPE . مثال شائع: ENUM تتحكم قيمه القاعدة: CREATE TYPE dayofweek AS ENUM ( 'Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday' ); بعدكدة يمكن استخدامه كـ column type. Real use cases: controlled statuses/categories مثل workflow state، priority، أو fixed classifications — عندما تكون القيم المسموح بها ثابتة ومناسبة لـ trade-offs بتاع ENUM. فحص user-defined types SELECT typname, typcategory FROM pg type; لمعرفة metadata لأعمدة جدول: SELECT column name, data type, udt name FROM information schema.columns WHERE table name = 'film'; مفيد جدًا عند استكشاف database غير مألوفة. User-defined functions إنشاء reusable database logic بـ CREATE FUNCTION . CREATE FUNCTION squared(i integer) RETURNS integer AS $$ SELECT i i; $$ LANGUAGE SQL; استخدامها: SELECT squared(5); -- → 25 Mental model: CREATE FUNCTION → package reusable database logic
